description: Three clothing photos in, a kidswear shoot out: a child from tiles in the whole outfit on white, four catalogue shots (full body, three-quarter, close-up, jump), and the same outfit on a second child with the same four shots. No photo of a real child needed.
markdownDescription:
## Kids Fashion Studio

Three clothing photos become a kidswear shoot: a child from tiles wearing the whole outfit on white, four catalogue shots — and the same outfit on a second child. No child's photo needed, no studio, no photographer.

1. **Clothing photos** — the top, the bottom, the shoes, each on a plain background. They never change.
2. **The kid** — pick the child from tiles: age, hair, skin, eyes. No photo of a real child.
3. **Styling notes + Light** — how the clothes are worn, and the studio light from tiles.
4. **Outfit notes + Kid card** — an AI writes the three garments down once; one full-body photo on white anchors every shot.
5. **Four shots** — full body, three-quarter, close-up, jump. Same child, same clothes, same white studio.
6. **Kid 2** — a second child from tiles in exactly the same outfit, the same four shots. The clothes are the product; the child is a choice.

data.text: An AI looks at the three photos and writes the outfit down in one precise paragraph: each piece, its colour, fabric and details. Every kid card and every shot quotes it, so the stripes, the straps and the soles never drift.

data.title: 5 · Outfit notes

data.text: Read this row left to right. The kid: pick the child from tiles — age, hair, skin, eyes — no photo of a real child needed, none stored. Kid card: one full-body photo of that child in all three pieces on white, the face and the clothes every shot is measured against. Then four shots, each with the card and the three clothing photos as references and its own fixed framing: full body, three-quarter, a close-up from slightly below, a jump. Kids move — the jump sells the clothes better than a pose.

data.text: The same row again with a second child from tiles — another age, another look: its own kid card in exactly the same clothes, then the same four shots. This is what a kidswear shop needs: the outfit is fixed, the child changes. Add a Kid 3 the same way, or swap the tiles here and rerun this row alone.

Outfit notes
data.userInput: Describe the outfit in the reference images.
data.systemPrompt: You write clothing descriptions for an image generator. Look at the reference images — each shows one piece of a child's outfit — and describe the whole outfit in ONE paragraph of 60–90 words, plain declarative English, one sentence per piece: garment type, colour, pattern, fabric, collar or straps, closures, pockets, cuffs, and for the shoes the material, sole and laces. Only what is visible. No brand names, no opinions, no bullet points, no commentary. Output only the paragraph.
